title: Companion v1 publishes state before events in each new world or life
before: Through the real game tick, an active audible cue in the first world produced SOUND (kind 4) followed by STATE (kind 1). The hub accepts a new world/life fence only on STATE, so it discarded that SOUND. The previous regular publication deadline could also defer the initial state after death, respawn or a world change.
change: Make the first state due on the transition tick. Send the state before any newly reported sound from that observation. A later chat on the same transport carries the established epoch. Ordinary publication remains at 5 Hz and event sequence numbers advance across boundaries.

test_scope.native: 8 hearing groups passed; native companion datagram suite passed.
test_scope.jkweb_source: 8 hearing groups passed in a native-compiled test harness using the portable callback.
cases: First state precedes a simultaneous ordinary weapon-hearing event. An intervening ordinary tick emits no extra state.
Death during a pending publication interval emits the new-life state before an immediately observed peer chat.
Respawn with a fresh audible cue emits the new-life state before its sound.
Game-world replacement emits the new-world state before subsequent chat. Event sequence numbers remain consecutive across all cases.
A callback accepting no output still permits ordinary processing of eight queued commands per native tick.

limits: These tests check emission order in a controlled world. Native datagrams and the browser bridge remain bounded and may drop records under backpressure or disconnection. The tests do not measure browser latency or claim end-to-end delivery in a live match.
